title: Owning stuff: measure cost in maintenance hours, not purchase price
summary: Sam argues the real cost of an asset is the maintenance time it demands, not what you paid for it. He went from owning cars and houses to renting and owning little, and says his mind is lighter and life more convenient, even if it earns him criticism.

principles.text: Judge the cost of owning something by the maintenance hours it consumes, not its purchase price.
principles.quote: Maintenance hours, not purchase price. That’s how much something cost.

principles.text: Owning fewer things removes a long tail of recurring chores: fixing, registering, renewing, insuring, updating, subscribing.
principles.quote: Fewer things to maintain. To fix. To register. To renew. Insure. Update. Subscribe.

principles.text: Optimize for a lighter mind and a more convenient life, even when conventional wisdom says you're losing money.
principles.quote: But what I do know definitely is that my mind is lighter and my life more convenient.

principles.text: Ignore criticism of unconventional choices like renting instead of buying a home when you're happier and possibly earning more.
principles.quote: I think I like make more money now not owning stuff.
